LLY's premium valuation is heavily reliant on dominating this space, making the Pfizer development a material threat to the long-term thesis. Exiting completely protects our remaining gains and frees up capital.

Actually, with $0 settled cash I cannot execute this buy today. I will flag this as a planned buy pending NVDA proceeds settling.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting NVDA fully as Jensen Huang's resignation invalidates the AI leadership thesis and intraday price action is pushing the position toward the 15% stop-loss.
recent_trades.reasoning: NVDA was purchased on the thesis of AI demand confirmation under Jensen Huang's visionary leadership. Today's news represents a fundamental change: Huang has resigned amid personal scandal, the board has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and Bernstein has cut its price target in half to $200. The stock is reportedly down 9% intraday from yesterday's close of $152.84, implying a price around ~$139. Combined with my entry at $173.42, this implies roughly a -20% drawdown — approaching or breaching the 15% stop-loss rule. There is no thesis left to hold: the specific driver I bought (AI GPU dominance under Huang) has been structurally disrupted. Interim CEO uncertainty will weigh on the stock for months. Full exit is warranted.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting NVDA immediately after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation - thesis invalidated and approaching stop-loss.
recent_trades.reasoning: Jensen Huang's resignation amid personal scandals is a fundamental, material change to the NVDA investment thesis. Huang was the visionary leader who built NVIDIA into the AI leader. His departure creates massive uncertainty around strategy, key customer relationships (hyperscalers), talent retention, and competitive moat sustainability. The stock was already down 14.86% from my entry and reports indicate an additional 9% decline today, which would breach the 15% stop-loss. Even if the stop-loss weren't a factor, the original thesis of NVDA as AI infrastructure leader was heavily predicated on Huang's leadership. Bernstein has already cut their price target in half to $200.

This is a speculative/thin-thesis position that I entered at confidence 5.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting AMD position as the rate-hike surprise creates meaningful headwinds for high-multiple semiconductor names despite today's positive Anthropic news.

Today's hot inflation print and Fed officials opening the door to a half-point hike is a material new macro development that directly pressures high-multiple growth/semiconductor stocks. AMD trades at a premium multiple and is most vulnerable to multiple compression in a rising rate environment. The positive news today (Anthropic stake, +2.66% stock move per headlines) is encouraging but the macro shift is a stronger force. With AMD at only 2.84% weight, the position is small, so exiting is a clean, low-cost decision that reduces growth exposure into a rate shock. I recently bought this, but the rate-hike catalyst is a specific new condition not present at entry.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting Disney to raise additional cash; low-conviction position vulnerable to consumer spending headwinds from higher inflation.
recent_trades.reasoning: DIS was purchased yesterday at confidence 5. The hot inflation print is particularly negative for consumer discretionary media spending. Disney's position is essentially flat, so this is a low-cost exit. The $600M earnings boost headline is interesting but one-time in nature. Raising cash to ~7.5% gives meaningful flexibility.

I'm trimming rather than exiting fully to maintain some exposure in case the institutional buying sustains the floor. Trimming to ~3% weight from ~5.8% frees meaningful cash.

recent_trades.reasoning: SLB was a speculative position initiated yesterday at confidence 5 based on undervaluation thesis. With October inflation data coming in hot and S&P futures falling sharply, energy services names face headwinds from potential rate hike fears offsetting any energy demand thesis. This is my lowest-conviction recent purchase and freeing up ~4% cash provides flexibility to act on better opportunities if the selloff deepens.
